summary: The snake's amṭay invitation is supplied at 59/44.
rationale: The matching full verse contains the same approach-and-spit invitation. This corrects its location without adding a duplicate quotation.

summary: Correct the verse containing ánnaqqa ... bəṯṯər eli
rationale: The supplied 65/490 has Annaqqa maṭi l aloho w bəṯr eli, matching the complete quotation. At 65/515 the speaker instead says bəṯr lu ǧanayḏi, followed by a different continuation.

summary: Correct the verse for the annual birth of a son
rationale: Despite the automatic found status, 88/150 only says Annaqla i=qəṣṣa čiroke yo. The next supplied verse, 88/151, has kul=šato komamṭyo abro and the matching birth context.

summary: Correct the verse of the snake’s invitation
rationale: At 59/19 the snake coils up, bursts and dies. At 59/44 it says amṭay, groyaqno b femux, the same invitation to come so it can spit into the boy’s mouth as in the glossary quotation.

summary: Restore fare from the cited verse
rationale: The supplied 61/247 reads tre fare, without x, and 61/246 already has baṣro daf fare. The supplied dictionary distinguishes faro, plural -e, Schaflamm (explicitly citing 61/246,247), from farxo, Junges von jeder Art von Tieren. This is a lexical consonant difference, not clitic or vowel normalization.

summary: Restore sie as the object of abnehmen
before: er nahm sich den Leuten ab
after: er nahm sie den Leuten ab
rationale: The supplied 29/284 reads er nahm sie den Leuten ab und holte sie zu sich. The preceding Turoyo names aʕ ʕeze, the goats; sich wrongly replaces the object pronoun sie.

summary: HD 48 am+mayani concerns bringing water rather than spouse-taking.
rationale: The explicit water theme contradicts III.2. No reconstruction or new translation is supplied.

summary: Number the inherited Detransitive transport example under new Detransitive sense 1.
rationale: The original Detransitive example is unnumbered; this connects it with the explicitly patient-subject Infectum without renumbering an existing sense.

summary: Objectless amṭay invites approaching.
rationale: The new III.5 separates its intransitive valency, already noted by '(komm)' in the existing translation.

summary: 64/32,241 illustrates price-yielding rather than transporting.
rationale: Saleable theme as subject and price/money as result establish the economic use. Preserve its original wording and both citations.

summary: 62/43 obtains the woman as an additional spouse.
rationale: The immediately following 62/44 makes spouse acquisition explicit; the existing example is refiled without duplication.

summary: File the water-bringing example under sense 1
rationale: The object am+mayani is water, so this is an example of holen, bringen (sense 1), not zum Gatten nehmen (sense 2). The proposal changes only the sense assignment; the abbreviated source does not establish a different stem.

summary: New box Infinitiv: example for sense 2 in Infinitiv (JL 7.8/4)

data.turoyo: maṭyo l mṭoyo
data.translation: wenn eine Wassermelone zur Reife gelangt ist

rationale: First separate Infinitiv placement for mṭoyo, already embedded in an existing finite-form example; not a new textual attestation.

summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 2 in Preterit-wa (JL 14.9/2)

data.turoyo: Aʕ=ʕənwe d maṭənwa, ak=karkuš, gqutfiwaynanne w gamṭiwaynanne baṭ=ṭaʕne lu=bayto.
data.translation: Wenn die Weintrauben reif geworden waren, die (Sorte) karkuš, dann pflückten wir sie und brachten sie in Tragtierlasten nach Hause.

summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC Ishaq Material culture/121)

data.turoyo: Bas uʕdo aʕ+ʕənwe k̬mitamṭən lu+bayto.
data.translation: But now the grapes get brought home.

summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (MAC Ishaq Material culture/49)

data.turoyo: Bonanwa kefe hul lalʕal, məd maṭyowa lfoṯa di+arʕo.
data.translation: They would build stones upwards, until it reaches the surface of the earth.

rationale: First sense-1 I Preterit-wa placement, following maṭyo vocalism; box is already established for sense 2 in batch 1. Formal contrast remains an editorial question.

summary: New box Infinitiv: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (58/83)

data.turoyo: Məlle: "Me qarʕux, d qoṭaʕnole w mu təmṭiyo dam maye du raqḏo gdamṭatte!"
data.translation: Der Sultan sprach: "Entweder werde ich dir den Kopf abschlagen, oder du holst das tanzende Wasser!"

rationale: First III Infinitiv box placement, təmṭiyo with dancing water as theme; do not derive an unprinted form.

summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (70/158)

data.turoyo: Əmmo: "Ḥoru baytux! Šxera xuderra i naqqayo an naʕime qəṭliwayle w lo maxəlṣatwayli mal lappaṯṯe w d lo məṭyowa i masale li daraǧaṯe!"
data.translation: Das füllen sprach: "Du Unglücksmensch! Hätten mich doch damals die Huben umgebracht und hättest du mich nicht aus ihren Klauen befreit und wäre doch die Sache nicht so weit gekommen!

rationale: Thin sense-1 Preterit-wa cell; contrary-to-fact achieved stage, distinct from habitual Infectum-wa.

summary: New sense 2b: (mit l-; einer Person eine Frau) eine Ehefrau verschaffen, verheiraten

data.label: 2b
data.gloss: (mit l-; einer Person eine Frau) eine Ehefrau verschaffen, verheiraten

rationale: The parents, rather than the groom, are the subject; ḥḏo is the spouse and the l-suffix identifies the son. Two attestations in one narrative.

summary: New sense 4: (mit l-ḥḏoḏe) zusammenbringen, versöhnen
rationale: Mediators bring antagonists into peace, explicitly preventing mutual killing; the repeated outcome establishes social reconciliation. This supersedes batch 1's extension-only treatment of JTM 4.4/19.

evidence.cite: MAC Murder in Kfarze, Ilyas’ summary of the story (Alyas d be Ġəzalo)/7
MAC Murder in Kfarze, Ilyas’ summary of the story (Alyas d be Ġəzalo)/8

summary: New sense 1: (Detrans.) gebracht werden
rationale: The existing Detransitive Preterit has no numbered sense; a patient-subject Infectum with grapes supports a shared transport sense. One new Infectum attestation.

summary: New sense 1d: (mit l-; auch l-ḥḏoḏe) geschlechtlich verkehren mit

data.label: 1d
data.gloss: (mit l-; auch l-ḥḏoḏe) geschlechtlich verkehren mit

rationale: Sexual participants are coded by l-, with explicit illicit intimacy in LuF and the son/stepmother question followed by divorce in PrS; no specific sexual act is inferred.

summary: New sense 5: (ohne Objekt, Imperativ) herkommen, nähertreten
rationale: Objectless amṭay invites the addressee to approach the snake. Already reflected by '(komm)' in the inherited Imperativ quotation, here given its own valency-based sense. One context, with corrected citation.

summary: New sense 6: (Ware als Subjekt) einen Preis erzielen, Geld einbringen

data.gloss: (Ware als Subjekt) einen Preis erzielen, Geld einbringen

rationale: The saleable armband yields price or money; it does not transport a theme. The same economic passage is already quoted at 64/32,241; reclassify it rather than duplicate.

summary: New sense 7: (mit ʕal rišo; ʕal qarʕo) über jemanden bringen, jemandem antun

data.gloss: (mit ʕal rišo; ʕal qarʕo) über jemanden bringen, jemandem antun

rationale: Repeated adverse-event themes combine with the affected person's possessed head, rather than a spatial destination.

summary: New sense 1e: (taqa als Subjekt; mit l-; ʕal) ausreichen, es mit jemandem aufnehmen können

data.label: 1e
data.gloss: (taqa als Subjekt; mit l-; ʕal) ausreichen, es mit jemandem aufnehmen können

rationale: Two strength-subject clauses compare capacity against an opponent, with l- and ʕal- alternation; this is an ability construction rather than an arrival event.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit-wa (Bilgic Die Rolle Məḏyaḏs im Tur Abdin/46)

rationale: First Preterit-wa example of established spouse-taking sense 2; referent uncertainty in the longer introduction is excluded.

summary: example for sense 2b in Infectum (Bilgic Hochzeit und Tod/2)

data.turoyo: Aṯile u maloxo, məlle li žənke, məlle: "Gədbenoləx abro. U yawmo, d amṭatle ḥḏo, gmoyəṯ."
data.translation: Es erschien ihm ... ihr der Engel und sagte zu der Frau, «ich werde dir ein Kind schenken und an dem Tag, an dem du ihn verheiratest, wird er sterben.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (Bilgic Hochzeit und Tod/12)

data.turoyo: Komər: "Kəḏaʕno, mərlalli, gmamṭət ḥḏo, gmayṯət."

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Hors 2/16)

data.translation: Sie ließen keinen Arzt in der Gegend aus, den sie nicht zu ihmgebracht hätten

data.translation: Er rief nach den Dienern: 'Sagt dem Oberkaufmann, ichhabe ihm ein (beschenk gebracht. Er soU sehen, ob es ihm gefällt.'

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 1.1/5)

data.turoyo: Bəṯr məd ... hawən aw warze, kul ḥəššabo, kəzzən mu bayto, kmanṭən af farḥe, waxt daf fuǧe gmanṭən fuǧe,
data.translation: Wenn die Melonenfelder reif geworden sind, gehen (die Midyader) jeden Samstag von zuhause und holen die Gurken, zur Zeit der Zuckermelonen holen sie Zuckermelonen.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (JTM 4.5/4)

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (JTM 5.1/43)

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JL 6.10/4)

summary: example for sense 4 in Infectum (MAC Murder in Kfarze, Ilyas’ summary of the story (Alyas d be Ġəzalo)/7)

data.turoyo: Omar, ‘Ṭroṯe noše baynoṯayna mamṭelan ləḥḏoḏe, gdowina bəšlomo, yani, dlo+quṭlina ḥḏoḏe, dlo+saymina mede bəḥḏoḏe’

data.turoyo: Ŭ bəṯr mraqqíwaynale, saymináwayna kore. Moṭənwa lu+qṭoro.
data.translation: And after that we would thin it, we would make grain bins. They would reach the ceiling.

rationale: Fills thin I Infectum-wa sense-1 cell to five; grain-bin antecedent discussed in note, unaltered edition translation retained.

summary: example for sense 1 in ko-Preterit (MAC NI Fingan Agha and Sultan Hasan/42)

data.turoyo: Zoxu ʕam Fәnǧā́n Aġá, kalkomaṭi qmi+qriṯo, qṭile, qṭəlle hən tre+tloṯo mə́nnestene ŭ gəquṭli híyestene, zoxu affele.
data.translation: Go to Finjan Agha, he has just arrived in front of the village, he has killed, they have killed some two-three of them even and they will kill him too, go to him!
data.ref: MAC NI Fingan Agha and Sultan Hasan/42

rationale: Thin I ko-Preterit cell; fused presentative plus completed-arrival form, with referent ambiguity retained.

summary: example for sense 1d in Preterit Intransitive (PrS 25/25)

data.turoyo: Omər: “Maṭiləx abri?” Əmmo: “Ya Bani sabʕa, harke lo maṭili, elo tamo maṭili.”
data.translation: »Hat mein Sohn dir beigewohnt?« fragte er. »O Löwenkönig«, entgegnete sie, »hier hat er mir nicht beigewohnt, aber dort«.

rationale: First Preterit Intransitive example for 1d; the edition's dialogue preserves here/there deixis without specifying an act.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 64/86)

data.turoyo: Omər: "Duš ḥozena bu bayto yo, mamtenala larke." Omər: "Duš", — u taʕlo.
data.translation: "Komm", erwiderte der Richter, "wir wollen sehen, ob sie zu Hause ist, und sie hierher bringen." "Vorwärts!" sagte der Fuchs.

rationale: Representative plain-t spelling mamtenala in Infectum; source spelling retained, without creating a new root.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (PrS 64/117)

data.turoyo: Mamtalle i kaččəke, aṯən lu bayto. Fayišo šato bu bayto, koṯalla an noše d ṭəlbila.
data.translation: So brachten sie das Mädchen nach Hause. Ein Jahr blieb sie dort Viele Leute kamen, um ihre Hand anzuhalten,

rationale: Representative plain-t Preterit Mamtalle in the same narrative as mamtenala; independent box/form evidence.

summary: example for sense 2b in Infectum (PrS 66/15)

data.turoyo: Omər: "Duš əzzan l gabayna, saymina məštuṯo, gmamṭenale aṯto l babi, mayiṯo emi."
data.translation: "Auf, lass uns nach unsrer Wohnung gehen; wir wollen ein Hochzeitsfest veranstalten und unserm Vater eine Frau zuführen; denn meine Mutter ist gestorben."

rationale: Thin cumulative III.2b Infectum cell; father's replacement wife is procured by others with explicit beneficiary.

summary: example for sense 2b in Infectum (26/85)

data.turoyo: Gmamṭenolux ḥḏo l goran diḏux w haṯe gdubinala ʕal oġur diḏa."
data.translation: Ich werde dir eine Frau holen, wie sie für dich paßt, und diese werden wir vergeben, so wie es ihr glück will."

rationale: Thin III.2b Infectum cell; uncle procures a suitable spouse for the addressed boy.

summary: example for sense 3 in Preterit (29/296)

data.turoyo: W ḥəlle walxalaṣ ḥzele: u abro, d mamṭele di qamayto, d mahzəmole, ġləble a tloṯaḥṣar ḥrene.
data.translation: Er sah schließlich, daß der Sohn der ersten, der, die er entführt hatte, die dreizehn anderen besiegte.

rationale: Thin procreation Preterit cell; father-subject construction with the first wife as maternal source.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (43/41)

data.turoyo: "Hn! W šxa ʕal u xabrano w lu fəkrano mamṭallalli lu ḥalano.
data.translation: "Hm... gerade wegen dieses Wortes und dieses Gedankens hat man mich ja in diesen Zustand gebracht.

rationale: Unusual expanded suffix chain with indefinite plural causers and a first-person patient; result-state endpoint remains a documented extension of bringing.

summary: example for sense 7 in Preterit (61/27)

data.turoyo: “E”, — mərre, — “aḥunone, l aloho mamṭele haṯe ʕal rišayna.
data.translation: "Eh", sprachen sie, "Brüder, Gott hat dies über uns gebracht.

rationale: First example of adverse-event construction III.7; deictic predicament and possessed-head affected target.

summary: example for sense 7 in Preterit (64/167)

data.turoyo: Faqaṭ ono kəḏʕono ebux. ʕAwwəl d əzzano l tamo, amar: "Ono u abro du šulṭono no w hiye u kačal yo w ʕəbraṯe kula mamṭole ʕal qarʕi, ḥatta d maṭino lu ḥalano."
data.translation: Aber ich weiß, was mit dir ist. Sobald wir dorthin kommen, sprich: Ich bin der Sohn des Sultans, und er ist der Kahlkopf, und er hat mir all diese abscheulichen Dinge angetan, bis ich in diesen Zustand geraten bin."

rationale: Second III.7 example with qarʕo rather than rišo, explicit adverse-theme resumption and a following reached-condition clause.

summary: example for sense 2b in Infectum (65/563)

data.turoyo: Mnaqaylux ḥḏo me lebux, aʕǧablux ḥḏo, d mamṭenuxyo w bəṯr gmobanno ḥoṯux!"
data.translation: und suche dir eine nach deinem Herzen aus, damit ich sie dir nehme, und dann werde ich deine Schwester heimführen!

rationale: Thin cumulative spouse-procurement Infectum cell; first-person procurer, second-person recipient and feminine spouse theme.

summary: example for sense 1 in ko-Preterit (30/54)

data.turoyo: W kmaṭino yawma taḥt i konayḏux w b aloho w buxat u daxilayḏux no.
data.translation: Und heute bin ich unter dein Zelt gekommen und bin, bei Gott und dir, dein Schutzgast.

rationale: Thin I ko-Preterit cell; first-person arrival supports a claim to hospitality/protection.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (64/146)

data.turoyo: Mqadamla las sawkoṯe lad dərrəhatanək, məlla: "Mṭawu l ḥḏoḏe w lo ṭorutu, d šofəʕ baynoṯauxu!"
data.translation: Sie ging zu jenem Gestrüpp, jenen dornen, und sprach: "Schließet euch zusammen und laßt ihn nicht zwischen euch durch!"

rationale: Thin I Imperativ cell; plural inanimate thorns reciprocally close a barrier through l ḥḏoḏe.

summary: example for sense 1e in Infectum (65/70)

data.turoyo: L Ṭahər Bage məlle l Zaynal Bage omər: "Aḥuno!" — "Hay ləbbe aḥuno!" Omər: "Mətyaqnat, mətyaqnat, i taqayḏan lə gməṭyo li ʕaskar tano.
data.translation: Tahir Bage sprach zu Zeinal Bage: "Bruder!" Ja Bruder?" Wir können es bestimmt nicht mit den Soldaten von dem da aufnehmen:'

rationale: First example of strength/capacity subsense I.1e; explicit opponent army with l-government.

summary: example for sense 1 in ko-Preterit (66/108)

data.turoyo: Lo kəmmat, kal komaṭi qum Gziro. Fayišo xud marke hul l Astəl. De u zlam nuxroyo, samyo yo.
data.translation: Aber nun war er zufällig gerade vor Gziro angelangt; es fehlte nur noch so viel wie von hier bis Astil. Aber der fremde ist ja blind.

rationale: Thin I ko-Preterit cell; completed arrival outside Gziro, independently of the traveler's recognition.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (69/317)

data.turoyo: Omər: "Ono greʕux, sofi, u darbayḏi raḥuqo yo, čike mʕawəq ruḥux! Klay məšwar, hul d əzzino, moṭeni čike d nuro. Me d maṭinux, edi malizat ste, ġamo layt!"
data.translation: "Derwisch, ich will dein Knecht sein! Mein Weg ist weit; wickele doch ein Biss eben langsam! Warte ein Weilchen, bis ich mir etwas Feuer geholt habe. Wenn ich wieder zu dir zurückgekommen bin, dann kannst du ja schneller wickeln und dann macht es nichts aus."

rationale: Unusual contracted first-person qaṭəl arrival plus second-person goal, used prospectively at a future boundary.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (71/50)

data.turoyo: Ənno am Mədwoye ʕariqi, bari me d mičoki b Bsorino, mṭawunne!
data.translation: Die Midiner sind geflohen, holt sie ein, ehe sie nach Bissorino hineinschlüpfen!

rationale: Thin I Imperativ cell; plural pursuit command with suffixed human goal, unlike III bringing.

summary: example for sense 2 in Part act. (73/359)

data.turoyo: Mlele i turayḏe, remune rabe xašune, maṭye w maḥatle riše w daməx!
data.translation: Erfüllte seine Handtasche mit großen, dicken, reifen Granatäpfeln und legte sich hin und schlief ein!

rationale: Thin ripening Part act. cell; plural attributive maṭye with pomegranates complements singular feminine and human-maturity examples.

rationale: The supplied 28/15 reads aṯi l bole. The numeral 1 in the glossary is a transcription slip for the preposition l.

summary: New idiom: mamṭele/mamṭe qanaʕa (mit l-; b-) ‘jemanden von etwas überzeugen’

data.headword: mamṭele/mamṭe qanaʕa (mit l-; b-) ‘jemanden von etwas überzeugen’
data.turoyo: W manṭalle laṣ ṣuroye qanaʕa b Šex Faṭhulla, kaʔinnahu u baxtayḏe ḥaqiqi yo, w bəṯər mena lə kowe bebaxtiye.
data.translation: Die Christen gewannen die Überzeugung, dass Schech Fatḥulla vertrauenswürdig war, und dass es danach keinen Verrat mehr geben würde.

rationale: Light verb plus qanaʕa, with l-recipient and b-topic; searched qanaʕa and found only a distinct ʔṯy construction elsewhere.

summary: New idiom: mamṭele/mamṭe qīm diḏ- (mit b-) ‘sich zufriedengeben, zufrieden sein’

data.headword: mamṭele/mamṭe qīm diḏ- (mit b-) ‘sich zufriedengeben, zufrieden sein’
data.turoyo: kmanṭət qim diḏux b tarte kefe? məlle e.
data.translation: du aber gibst dich mit zwei Steinen zufrieden? Er sagte: Ja.

rationale: New collocation listing, supported by JTM 1.1/79 and the inherited III.1 Preterit 62/355; no duplicate numbered sense.

summary: New idiom: mamṭele/mamṭe l-u=darbo ‘auf den rechten Weg bringen’

data.headword: mamṭele/mamṭe l-u=darbo ‘auf den rechten Weg bringen’
data.turoyo: komər yatu mrakzile, manṭalle lu darbo, w krəzle aʕlayye, hawxa yo hawxa yo hawxa yo.
data.translation: Er ließ sich nieder, disziplinierte sie und brachte sie wieder auf den rechten Weg, und er predigte ihnen: (Es verhält sich) so und so und so.

rationale: Figurative path collocation grounded in discipline and preaching; exact l-darbo search found no existing listing.

summary: New idiom: mamṭele/mamṭe ḏ̣arbo (mit ʕal) ‘einen Schlag gegen jemanden richten’

data.headword: mamṭele/mamṭe ḏ̣arbo (mit ʕal) ‘einen Schlag gegen jemanden richten’
data.turoyo: komər manṭele i ḏ̣arbo ʕal u ʕammo, d maʕle d muḥela b ḥaṣe du ʕammo,
data.translation: Er zielte einen Schlag auf den Onkel, er wollte (den Speer) hochheben und ihn in den Rücken des Onkels stoßen

rationale: Recurrent light-verb construction at JTM 5.2/91–94; aiming is supported, successful landing is not entailed. Existing mḥy blow idiom uses a different verb.

summary: New idiom: mamṭele/mamṭe kemayiyat (mit ʕal) ‘an jemandem Fehler finden’

data.headword: mamṭele/mamṭe kemayiyat (mit ʕal) ‘an jemandem Fehler finden’
data.turoyo: Mṭíwayna k̇emayiyat aʕlayye.
data.translation: We would find fault with them.

rationale: New light-verb collocation with fault noun and ʕal-target; supplied judgments concern specific men's attributes, not a separate general disparage sense.

summary: New idiom: mamṭele/mamṭe ṣabər diḏ- ‘sich die Wartezeit vertreiben’

data.headword: mamṭele/mamṭe ṣabər diḏ- ‘sich die Wartezeit vertreiben’
data.turoyo: Kmamṭe ṣabər diḏe bawxa, qut kəmlo i šato.
data.translation: mit solchen Dingen vertrieb er sich die Zeit, bis das Jahr (das sie sich ausbedungen hatte) zu Ende gehen würde.

rationale: New patience/waiting collocation; the possessed ṣabər and bounded waiting period support getting through the wait, without asserting exhaustion of patience.

summary: New idiom: mamṭele/mamṭe xabro (mit ʕal) ‘die Rede auf etwas bringen’

data.headword: mamṭele/mamṭe xabro (mit ʕal) ‘die Rede auf etwas bringen’
data.turoyo: Naqqa ḥreto mamṭelan u xabro ʕal u zoġo.
data.translation: Dann brachten wir die Rede wieder auf den Hahn.

rationale: Light verb plus discourse noun and ʕal-topic; differs formally from existing baḥs d- and maṯlo collocations.

summary: New idiom: ruḥo maṭyo l-nḥiro ‘in Todesangst sein’

data.turoyo: Annaqqa mayəṯno! Annaqqa maṭyo i ruḥo l nḥiri!
data.translation: jetzt bin ich tot, die Seele ist mir schon bis zur Nase gekommen!

rationale: Mined from the reader's question: whole-clause soul-to-nostrils image expresses mortal fear. One attestation; no independent fear sense of the verb.

summary: New idiom: mamṭele/mamṭe ruḥo (mit b-) ‘Lebensodem wiedergeben’

data.turoyo: Komər bi saʕayayo a tre abnayḏa l aloho mamṭele ruḥo appe, qayimi kul ḥa, hawile xanxolo d dahwo b dukṯe di nḥarto d nḥirənne.
data.translation: In diesem Augenblick gab Gott ihren beiden Söhnen wieder Lebensodem. Sie standen auf, aber jedem von ihnen war ein goldener Ring an der Stelle entstanden, so man sie geschlachtet hatte.

rationale: Light verb plus life-breath theme, with b-goal and restored boys; specific collocation, without treating every fetching-a-soul clause as resurrection.

summary: New idiom: mamṭele/mamṭe (X) l-bol- ‘sich erinnern; jemanden an etwas erinnern’

data.headword: mamṭele/mamṭe (X) l-bol- ‘sich erinnern; jemanden an etwas erinnern’
data.turoyo: Omər i naqqa d amṭele i dukṯo d Gulbaran l bole, lu zlamano marfele ḥaṣra w kadar rabo.
data.translation: Als er ihm den Ort des Gulbaran in Erinnerung brachte, gab er einen Seufzer von sich und wurde sehr betrübt.

rationale: Cognitive-goal collocation, paired with the existing 11/153 remembrance example and distinct from intransitive ʔṯy l-bol-. One new quotation covers reminding, without duplicating the inherited remembrance text.

summary: New idiom: mamṭele/mamṭe nəqṣaniye (mit ʕal) ‘jemandem einen Makel anheften’

data.headword: mamṭele/mamṭe nəqṣaniye (mit ʕal) ‘jemandem einen Makel anheften’
data.turoyo: M ʕal aṯe ono lə gbaʕno d mamṭeno nəqṣaniye aʕli w ʕal i zʕurtaṯe, d huluxli yo i aṯtayḏi, bi dukṯayḏi dan noše d l əmmi ašər, latla babo.
data.translation: Ich möchte daher vermeiden, daß mir und dem Mädchen, das du mir gegeben hast, meiner Frau, sich ein mangelanheftet; damit in meiner Heimat die Leute nicht sagen: Sie hat keinen Vater.

rationale: New blemish-noun collocation with affected ʕal-targets; one context, distinct from generic bringing of an adverse event.

summary: New idiom: mamṭele/mamṭe šəkriye (mit me-) ‘dankbar sein, Dank ausdrücken’

data.headword: mamṭele/mamṭe šəkriye (mit me-) ‘dankbar sein, Dank ausdrücken’
data.turoyo: Məlle: "Annaqqa mamṭi i šəkriyayḏux m aloho.
data.translation: Er sprach: "So, nun sei dankbar gegen Gott!

rationale: New possessed-thanks collocation; edition wording retained and me-government recorded, not silently changed to a recipient l-.

summary: New idiom: gawo maṭi l-bəṯre ḥaṣo ‘großen Hunger haben’

data.headword: gawo maṭi l-bəṯre ḥaṣo ‘großen Hunger haben’
data.turoyo: Gawi maṭi l bəṯre ḥaṣi!
data.translation: Der Magen hängt mir schon ganz schief.

rationale: New whole-clause hunger hyperbole; literal image is identified in the note, while the edition's different German image is retained verbatim.

summary: Full-batch decisions distinguish I intransitive arrival/ripening from III transitive bringing. mamṭ-, amṭ-, maṭṭ- and Midyat manṭ- alternate; the independent mṭy 2 lookup confirms semantic and morphological overlap, but this batch does not merge entries.

Routine counts support I arrival and III bringing as dominant uses. They are supplied aggregates for the large root, not additional individually inspected evidence and not totals to add again in later batches.

l- introduces destinations, recipients or scalar endpoints according to construction. The parents' procuring a wife for their son motivates III.2b; a bride as theme alone does not force this subsense.
qīm and qanaʕa are light-verb collocations. The paired mawballe w manṭalle ḥḏoḏe at JTM 5.2/94 describes reciprocal combat movement; it does not prove ellipsis of ḏ̣arbo.

JL 7.8/3 and /4 are already quoted under I Infectum and Preterit Intransitive respectively, in a different editorial rendering. Do not duplicate or overwrite those quotations. The Infinitiv and Preterit-wa placements add filing coverage, not newly discovered source text.
Repeated reader claims that 24/320 and 26/63 require movement from III.1 are incorrect: the actual input already files both as III.2. No correction is issued.
Batch 2 supersedes batch 1's extension-only reconciliation decision: mediators and explicit peace/nonviolence establish III.4. No earlier output is rewritten; the cumulative entry records the change.
I.1d groups reciprocal illicit sexual contact and l-marked sexual partnership. Desire in LuF does not entail consummation; PrS here/there deixis is retained without specifying intercourse type.
Detransitive mitamṭən promotes grapes as patient subject and omits the carrier. Human indefinite plural carriers elsewhere remain active III, even when German uses man.

Abandoned maṭ… tokens in Lahdo are explicitly rejected as complete forms. Overt mamṭ-/amṭ-/manṭ- and constructional baḥs evidence support provisional III filing, while short mṭ- alone often cannot distinguish mṭy 2.
The MAC Hanna Dewo/48 context independently confirms batch 1's HD 48 water-example move to III.1. The source's English translation is retained, not substituted into the inherited fragment.
Repeated claims of zero spouse-taking Preterit examples are stale: the parsed entry already has two and the previous batch added one. This batch adds only two more, filling that cell to five.
III.2b is retained for explicit third-party spouse procurement at PrS 66/15, 26/85 and 65/563. The exact inherited 24/320 has ambiguous agent segmentation, so its established III.2 placement remains.

Objectless amṭay, economic price-yielding, and adverse-event bringing receive III.5–7 without renumbering I.1–2 or III.1–4. Existing examples are moved by id where they already supply the needed quotation.

The armband, not the newborn daughter, is the referent yielding sale proceeds at 64/32 and 64/241: sale is intended to support both mother and daughter. The earlier inherited quotation is preserved, while its semantic filing is corrected.

qīm/qəm consent merges with the collocation introduced in batch 1; no additional numbered consent sense or second idiom is created. baḥs, ḥəǧǧe, waṣiye and ʕayno maṭyo examples are also already listed.
Plain-t mamt- spellings recur in PrS 64 and 35/28; represent them as edition spellings, not evidence that all emphatic/non-emphatic roots should merge.
Several supplied edition translations omit the bringing clause, including PrS 81/25 and 24/243. They are analyzed but not quoted as examples. gmaṭi at 66/164 is not silently labeled ko-Preterit.
Most routine cells are now adequately populated. Additional contextual bringing and repeated bride-taking passages are not added merely because the reader used baseline thin-cell counts.
Is mṭoyo at JL 7.8/4 an Infinitiv used as a cognate maturity noun, or should the separate Infinitiv placement be revised?
Clarify kadd and the referent of -ne in Hors 3/24; neither an earnings sense nor a new collocation is established by the supplied context.
Confirm kmuṭele šḥanṯo at JTM 1.5/46: agreement, l-suffix referent, and I versus reduced transitive analysis.
Confirm root and segmentation of kmanṭe ʕar ruḥe + d-clause (JTM 4.3/6); no separate sense is published on the uncertain analysis.
Confirm segmentation of amṭallaleyo, mamṭənne, manṭənanne, and the identical male/female-address amṭiye forms; no gender neutralization is asserted.
Verify the distinct JL 12.13.14 inherited ko-Preterit quotation against the edition; JL 15.6/14 alone cannot establish that its citation is wrong.
Does III.3 cover both fathering and giving birth? The inherited Infectum kul šato ko-mamṭyo abro has a female subject, while the current III.3 gloss asks about men.
Is the water-bringing fragment HD 48, currently under III.2, an editorially misplaced example? Its overt am+mayani supports III.1; the correction retains its original text.
Does LuF 2/43 imply intended intercourse or broader illicit sexual contact? Confirm the semantic limits of I.1d without expanding PrS 25/25 deixis into a specific act.
Confirm maṭyowa versus məṭyowa at MAC Ishaq Material culture/49: distinct Preterit-wa/Infectum-wa bases or dialectal vowel leveling?
Clarify the agreement of ants Gməṭyola at LuF 3/75 and fear moṭéwaylan zuḥṯo at MAC Hanna Dewo/88; neither is used to establish a new paradigm form.
Confirm the target and register of kemayiyat ʕal- and whether mamṭe ṣabər can express other phases of patience outside PrS 18/29.
Resolve agent and patient suffixes in əmṭúṭuwayle, mamṭenanxu, mamṭallallan and mamṭiyulle; do not infer masculine human reference solely from -lle.
Check the untranslated bringing clauses at PrS 7/19 and 50/6, and the incomplete translation around PrS 28/8, before considering them as publication examples.
Confirm objectless amṭay in 59/44 as an invitation rather than an omitted reflexive patient, and verify its replacement of the inherited citation 59/19 against the edition.
Resolve the suffix and agent structure of amṭannanne in 24/320 before assigning it to third-party procurement rather than established spouse-taking.
Does maṭyono lašanux at 61/315 express promised-spouse transfer or a Detransitive interpretation? The provisional I arrival/receipt analysis is not used to create another sense.
Confirm gmaṭi at 66/164 and məṭyowa at 70/158: prospective qaṭəl versus dialectal Infectum and vowel leveling.
Confirm whether bringing life-breath, soul reaching nostrils, and the belly/back hunger image are conventional collocations beyond these individual contexts.
Clarify the missing edition translation of təmṭiyo as a nominal form at 58/83: the supplied German paraphrases the whole demand as a finite clause.
Resolve the final -l in Maṭil and the suffixes in mamṭallalli, mamṭannanne and maṭinux without normalizing the supplied text.
Correct zuf to auf
rationale: The German separable verb is aufheben; zuf is a typographical error in the description of picking up the boy.

summary: Correct the spelling of Frühstück

summary: Correct the plural Mandeln

summary: Progress through viewed images (Hors 2/9,25), marriageable age (Hors 2/70), vineyard bearing age (JTM 1.1/45), and spatially spreading seed retain reaching/attainment.
Ripening extends from fruit to grain and grass; melon fields stand metonymically for their produce.
Rescuing people from danger is contextual bringing out of a hostile group; no independent rescue meaning established. Likewise bringing a burner to level three retains a scalar endpoint.
Warmth reaching people is a possible thermal participant extension; kmuṭele and agreement with šḥanṯo remain unresolved, so no example or new sense is published.
Bringing revived people l ḥḏoḏe permits social reconciliation in context; a distinct lexical reconciliation sense is not demonstrated.

Batch 1 treated the revived people's bringing together as a contextual reconciliation extension. Batch 2's explicit mediators and peace clauses now establish III.4; JTM 4.4/19 is a compatible earlier instance, without adding its uncertain quotation.
Age as subject and a numerical age endpoint are scalar attainment, continuous with inherited I.1b and the existing marriageable-age construction; no new numbered age sense.
The attributive Part act. mṭiṯo describes a mature daughter, extending the existing ripeness sense to a human participant.
Messages reach human recipients; fear may similarly reach an experiencer, though agreement and reduced transitive alternatives remain unresolved.
ʕal-person marks responsibility in PrS 6/24, comparable to inherited l-aloho ... eli at 65/515; government differs, while the underlying matter reaching a responsible party is already represented.

Approaching death, reaching a liturgical stage, turning to a narrative topic, and a bride coming to the intended spouse all retain a reached endpoint. Do not infer completed death or an independent entitlement meaning.
A patient brought to an adverse condition remains causing a reached state. This differs from III.7's possessed-head affected target.
29/296 has paternal procreation; the inherited 88/150 has maternal childbearing. The shared production-of-a-child meaning needs an editorial decision about the existing male-only question.
